channels.regime: Strong ISM demand/prices, oil/product inflation and market pricing for further Fed tightening keep policy relief limited.
US 10Y ~5.19%, 30Y ~5.48% and Japan 10Y ~3.115% make global duration/capital scarcity the dominant valuation constraint.
AI/project-finance dispersion remains active; fresh CCC OAS is still a verification gap.
Physical AI/grid demand remains strong, but funding, interconnection, permitting and cost of capital are stricter filters.
Crude is again elevated above the prior relief zone, but inventories and partial rerouting argue against treating every spike as permanent scarcity.
Distillate stocks remain structurally low and diesel tightness is expected to persist; refined products are a stronger inflation signal than crude alone.
High global yields and energy inflation constrain broad risk appetite despite selective AI/equity resilience.
Gold is tactically pressured by higher real/nominal yields and a firmer dollar despite structural fiscal/geopolitical support.
5%+ long yields materially increase financing and hurdle rates; prefer contracted, cash-generative or strongly sponsored AI infrastructure.
Trade-truce extension reduced one tail risk but does not demonstrate a repair in household/private credit or domestic demand transmission.
Rare-earth/yttrium bottlenecks remain unresolved after the summit and directly affect aerospace, power and semiconductor supply chains.
Realizable MW remains constrained by interconnection, generation, transmission, cooling/water and now a higher financing cost.

notes: Daily Investment Brief did not expose reliable numeric dashboard values in this run; no placeholder was inferred. MacroMicro also did not provide a reliable supplemental reading.
Official August ISM remains the latest monthly release: Manufacturing 54.6 and Services 55.4. Manufacturing Prices 71.1; Services Prices 72.6.
The key regime change is the combination of multi-decade-high sovereign yields and renewed energy/product inflation, not rates or oil in isolation.
US distillate inventories remain structurally tight even as crude inventories rose; continue to separate crude, refined products, LNG and freight.
The US-China summit extended the truce but did not verify a durable resolution of rare-earth, tariff or advanced-technology restrictions.
Creator/social claims remain zero-weight until independently verified; the claimed 'largest QQQ transaction ever' remains unverified.
Fresh authoritative CCC OAS, same-contract US crack spreads and standalone 6742UW terms remain research gaps.

Live Desk canonical cross-check confirms rates-led tightening with incomplete credit transmission, weak broad participation versus stronger AI/semis, and refined-product inflation risk. These diagnostics do not directly change stock scores without an explicit Power Stack sensitivity.

forwardView.baseCase: Global duration and energy inflation remain the two dominant cross-asset constraints. Selective physical AI/grid and cash-generative energy exposures can outperform, but broad duration risk needs yields and oil/product inflation to stabilize together.
forwardView.dollar: Bias remains firm while US growth/prices, oil inflation and front-end/long-end yields stay elevated.
forwardView.rates: US 10Y ~5.19%, 30Y ~5.48% and JGB 10Y ~3.115% are the tripwires. A durable risk-on broadening needs long yields to retreat, not merely equities to tolerate them for a session.
forwardView.equities: Prefer funded/cash-generative AI infrastructure, power/grid and selective security over unprofitable duration. Do not chase strong themes at stretched prices.
forwardView.energy: Treat crude, diesel/products, LNG and shipping separately. Product tightness is currently the cleaner inflation signal.
forwardView.gold: Structural case remains, but tactical confirmation requires real/nominal yields and DXY to roll over together.
forwardView.nextCatalyst: US inflation/labour data, Treasury supply/auction follow-through, Middle East supply developments, product inventories/cracks and company-specific AI/grid funding evidence.
